candidates.tagline: Elon called it Tesla's 'best product ever' — it's now selling worse than the Ford Edsel
candidates.story: A Bloomberg analysis published July 22, 2026 showed Tesla's Cybertruck is a bigger commercial failure relative to targets than Ford's 1957 Edsel — the historical benchmark for automotive flops — after Musk projected 250,000 annual sales but the truck managed only 3,519 deliveries in Q1 2026 and fewer than 8,000 units through May 2026, with stock falling 18% in a week.
candidates.why_funny: The man who promised Tesla's 'best product ever' built a stainless steel truck that looks like a refrigerator tipped on its side and sold it at one-sixth the promised annual rate — to fewer people, proportionally, than even the Edsel.
candidates.alt: A Foundation Series Tesla Cybertruck photographed at dusk in South San Jose, showing the flat angular stainless steel body, geometric headlight strip, and completely straight panel lines with no visible curves

candidates.tagline: Audi's $90,000 Q9 projects turn-signal arrows onto the road, in case your eyes are on the asphalt
candidates.story: Audi revealed its 2027 Q9 flagship at $90,000+ in late July 2026 with a headline feature that uses Digital Matrix LEDs to project animated turn-signal arrow graphics directly onto the pavement when signaling — plus a 'welcome rug' of light cast on the ground when you open the door — which reviewers at Men's Journal immediately called 'solving problems nobody had.'
candidates.why_funny: Audi engineered an animated arrow light show on the street in case pedestrians who somehow missed the turn indicator — a device unchanged in principle since 1939 — are looking down at the asphalt instead.
candidates.alt: The 2027 Audi Q9 luxury SUV projecting a glowing animated turn-signal arrow graphic onto dark asphalt from its Digital Matrix LED system, photographed from the rear quarter
